audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate fields claim Ragnarok turns Olaf's basic attacks into true damage. It does not. Riot's text: 'Olaf passively gains increased armor and magic resist. He can activate this ability to become immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking.' The true damage in his kit is Reckless Swing (E) — one ability, 325 range, 11s at rank 1, which also costs him health and refunds it on a kill.
audit.why: This is the difference between 'never fight him in R' and 'dodge one short-range ability'. A player who believes his autos are true damage will give up the mist fight entirely, when in reality Hallowed Mist's bonus armour and MR work perfectly well against everything except Reckless Swing. Ragnarok's real threat is the disable immunity, which blanks Needlework's slow.
audit.corrected: True damage attributed to Reckless Swing; Ragnarok described as passive resists plus disable immunity while he keeps attacking.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart reads Skill / Olaf / Olaf / Skill / Skill / Olaf / Olaf, but whys[0] says he out-trades levels 1-3, whys[3] calls 4-5 'your worst window', whys[4] and whys[5] hand 6 and first item to Gwen, and whys[6] says 'genuinely even'.
audit.why: At 49.2% this is a near-even lane with a clean shape: Olaf owns everything before Hallowed Mist, Gwen owns 6 through first item, and it levels out after.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Olaf / Olaf / Olaf / Olaf / Gwen / Gwen / Skill in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Fight when his R is down' with no number, and Undertow's reset is described without its base cooldown.
audit.why: Ragnarok is 100/90/80s, Undertow a flat 9s (reset entirely on pickup), Tough It Out 16s at rank 1 and Reckless Swing 11s. The 9-second axe is why denying the pickup matters so much — without it he waits the full nine.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to the spikes, whys and cooldown breakdown.

audit.why: His attack speed AND lifesteal scale with MISSING health, so a low Olaf is a stronger Olaf — chipping him down without killing him actively arms him. That reframes every 'grind him out' line on the page.
audit.corrected: Stated in the late paragraph and the cooldown breakdown.

edits.after: Genuinely even — your percent-HP shred and healing scale, but Ragnarok's disable immunity blanks your slows and Reckless Swing's true damage ignores Mist's resists, so whoever lands their window wins.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still his — you're a melee with no untargetability yet against his slow-and-chase, so farm safely and wait for 6. At 6 the lane flips: Needlework's slow plus your full Q-W-E rotation lets you drop Hallowed Mist as he commits, deny his axe pickup, and snip the percent-max-HP off his big bruiser bar while your abilities heal you back. The trap is his Ragnarok — once it's up he's CC-immune so your needle and E slows do nothing, and his empowered autos turn true, so bait the R or only fight when it's on cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still his — a melee with no untargetability against slow-and-chase — so farm safely and wait for 6. At 6 the lane flips: Needlework's slow plus your full Q-W-E rotation lets you drop Hallowed Mist as he commits, deny the axe pickup so Undertow sits its full nine seconds, and snip the percent-max-HP off his bruiser bar while your abilities heal you back. The trap is Ragnarok — for 100 seconds at rank 1 he can be immune to disables while he keeps attacking, so your slows do nothing. Bait it or fight while it is down.

edits.before: Your Nashor's-into-Riftmaker spike turns extended fights your way — percent-HP Snip Snip! plus your ability healing grinds his lifesteal bruiser bar down harder the more HP he builds, and Mist's resists blunt his physical autos. But never forget Ragnarok: it strips your slows with CC-immunity and converts his autos to true damage that ignores Mist's bonus armor/MR and out-paces your healing, so a committed Olaf can still trade you down inside your own fog. Pick fights when his R is down, kite with E and needles around his axe range, and the lane stays a coinflip that tilts to whoever lands their window — exactly the even matchup it is.
edits.after: Your Nashor's-into-Riftmaker spike turns extended fights your way — percent-HP Snip Snip! plus ability healing grinds his bar down harder the more HP he builds, and Mist's resists blunt his physical autos, which are NOT true damage. Two things to respect. Ragnarok strips your slows with disable immunity for as long as he keeps swinging, and Reckless Swing (E, 11s) is real true damage that ignores those resists. Worse, Berserker Rage gives him attack speed and lifesteal off MISSING health, so a half-dead Olaf is the dangerous one. Fight when R is down, kite around his 9-second axe, and the lane stays the coinflip it is.

edits.before: Track Olaf's Ragnarok: CC/slow-immune — your R slow won’t hold him. Mist it. When it is down — Snip him in your mist.
edits.after: Ragnarok (R, 100s) is disable immunity, not true damage — his true damage is Reckless Swing (E, 11s). Mist's resists still work.

edits.before: - Olaf Ragnarok: matchup-defining — CC/slow-immune — your R slow won’t hold him. Mist it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Ragnarok (R): 100/90/80s — immune to disables while he keeps attacking, so Needlework will not hold him. - Undertow (Q): a flat 9s, reset by picking the axe up. - Reckless Swing (E): 11s of TRUE damage.

notes: The kit file gives Undertow a derived 'grounding' flag, but Riot's description says it reduces armour and move speed only. Per the trust-the-description rule I did not claim it stops Skip 'n Slash — worth a human check, since a grounding axe would change every escape line here.
